rounds.t: Bone cell biology and upper limb injuries

q.s: Which enzyme do osteoblasts use to catalyze bone mineralization in an alkaline environment?
e: Correct. Bone ALP, osteocalcin and type I procollagen propeptides measure osteoblast activity.

q.s: Osteoclasts arise from which lineage?
Osteoprotegerin decreases bone resorption by:
o: Acting as a decoy receptor that binds RANKL

q.s: Low, intermittent PTH levels (as with teriparatide) have which effect on bone?
Why does postmenopausal estrogen deficiency increase osteoporosis risk?
o: Estrogen normally induces osteoclast apoptosis and protects osteoblasts; loss increases remodeling and resorption

q.s: A carpenter has pain near the lateral epicondyle that worsens with wrist extension. Diagnosis?
Golfer's elbow results from repetitive:
A child falls on an outstretched hand and fractures the clavicle. Where do clavicle fractures most commonly occur?
e: Correct. The weakest point is at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds.

q.s: In a clavicle fracture, the lateral fragment is displaced:
o: Downward by arm weight and medially rotated by arm adductors
e: Wrong. Medial fragment rises with SCM.

q.s: A pregnant woman has tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers that worsens at night. Tapping over the wrist reproduces the tingling. Why is sensation over the thenar eminence spared?
o: The palmar cutaneous branch enters the hand outside the carpal tunnel
The ulnar nerve supplies the thenar skin
e: Correct. Carpal tunnel syndrome; positive Tinel sign.

q.s: Which condition is associated with carpal tunnel syndrome?
e: Correct. Also pregnancy, RA, diabetes, acromegaly and dialysis-related amyloidosis.

q.s: Holding the wrists fully flexed for 60 seconds reproduces tingling in the lateral fingers. This is:
A 19-year-old man punches a wall and has pain over the back of his hand near the little finger. Which fracture is most likely?
Guyon canal syndrome is compression of which nerve?
A man with Crohn disease has fever, flank pain and an inguinal mass. Extending his hip worsens lower abdominal pain. Which organism is most commonly isolated?
e: Wrong. Possible, but not most common.
Correct. Psoas abscess with positive psoas sign.

q.s: Tuberculous spondylitis spreading to the psoas muscle is called:
What is the treatment for a psoas abscess?
Which marker reflects osteoblastic activity?
e: Wrong. Not a bone cell marker.

q.s: Osteoclasts dissolve bone by secreting:
RANKL is expressed by which cells?
A football player is hit on the lateral side of his knee with his foot planted. Which injury pattern is the "unhappy triad"?
e: Correct. (Lateral meniscus involvement is actually more common with ACL/MCL injury.)

q.s: A carpet layer has swelling directly in front of the kneecap. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Anterior knee pain without swelling.

q.s: A 65-year-old woman with osteoarthritis of the knee has a fluid-filled swelling behind the knee. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa communicating with the joint.

q.s: A 25-year-old woman has sharp chest pain that worsens with deep breaths and reproducible tenderness over the costosternal junctions. ECG is normal. Diagnosis?
A new mother has pain at the radial styloid. Pain increases when she makes a fist around her thumb and deviates the wrist ulnarly. Which tendons are involved?
o: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
e: Correct. De Quervain tenosynovitis; positive Finkelstein test.

q.s: A 62-year-old man of Northern European descent cannot fully extend his ring and little fingers. Thick cords are palpable in the palm. Cause?
o: Fibroblastic proliferation of the superficial palmar fascia
e: Wrong. Trigger finger or De Quervain.

q.s: A smooth swelling on the dorsum of the wrist glows when a light is shone through it. Diagnosis?
o: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

q.s: A runner has lateral knee pain that worsens during runs. Which structure is rubbing against the lateral femoral epicondyle?

After a tibial shaft fracture, a man has severe leg pain that worsens with passive toe flexion and a tense, swollen calf. Pulses are present. Which complication is most likely, and what are its late consequences?
o: Compartment syndrome; rhabdomyolysis and acute tubular necrosis
e: Correct. Pulses are often preserved early.

q.s: In compartment syndrome, which findings are late signs of irreversible damage?
e: Wrong. Not the listed late sign.

q.s: A military recruit has diffuse tenderness along the medial tibia that worsens with running. What causes this condition?
o: Bone resorption outpacing formation in the tibial cortex
e: Correct. Medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints).

q.s: An overweight nurse has heel pain that is worst with her first steps in the morning. Diagnosis?
A woman has dull, constant unilateral facial pain that worsens with chewing, ear pain and limited jaw opening. Diagnosis?
Which population is at increased risk of De Quervain tenosynovitis?
o: New mothers lifting babies and frequent thumb texters
e: Correct. Also golfers and racquet sport players.

q.s: Compartment syndrome may be caused by:
Popliteal cysts are most commonly related to:
o: Chronic joint disease such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis

q.s: Which statement about the unhappy triad is correct?
o: It results from a medial force on the knee
It occurs with the foot off the ground
Lateral meniscus involvement is actually more common than medial with ACL and MCL injury

q.s: Costochondritis is more common in which population?
Ganglion cysts most commonly occur:
o: On the dorsal side of the wrist

q.s: Which pair matches the knee test to the structure?

rounds.t: Childhood musculoskeletal conditions and pediatric fractures

q.s: A 3-year-old cries and holds her arm slightly flexed and pronated after her father swung her by the hands. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. The immature annular ligament slips over the radial head.

q.s: A 13-year-old basketball player has a painful bump below the kneecap after a growth spurt. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Traction apophysitis of the tibial tuberosity.

q.s: A 16-year-old female runner has anterior knee pain worse after prolonged sitting. Diagnosis?
A newborn delivered breech has a "clunk" on hip examination. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
e: Correct. Developmental dysplasia of the hip.
Wrong. Cartilage is not ossified until 4–6 months.

q.s: Which maneuvers screen for developmental dysplasia of the hip?
A 6-year-old boy has a painless limp that has developed over weeks and mild hip pain. Initial x-ray is normal. Which condition is most likely?
e: Correct. Idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head (ages 5–7, boys).

q.s: A 12-year-old obese boy has knee pain and walks with an externally rotated leg. X-ray shows the femoral head displaced relative to the neck. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. "Ice cream slipping off a cone."

q.s: A child falls and an x-ray shows an incomplete fracture that fails on the tension side with the compression side intact. This is a:
An axial force on a child's distal radius causes the cortex to buckle on the compression side with the tension side intact. This is a:
Achondroplasia is caused by:
o: Constitutive activation of FGFR3, inhibiting chondrocyte proliferation

q.s: Why do patients with achondroplasia have a relatively large head?
o: Skull bones form by endochondral ossification only

q.s: Most cases of achondroplasia occur:
o: Sporadically, associated with increased paternal age
In children of two affected parents

q.s: Which risk factor is associated with developmental dysplasia of the hip?
Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease has which sex ratio?
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis results from:
o: Increased axial force displacing the epiphysis relative to the femoral neck
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head

q.s: Osgood-Schlatter disease is caused by:
o: Repetitive strain and chronic avulsion of the tibial tuberosity ossification center

q.s: Achondroplasia is the most common cause of:
In radial head subluxation, which ligament slips over the head of the radius?
Patellofemoral syndrome is worsened by:
o: Prolonged sitting or weight-bearing on a flexed knee

q.s: Which statement about greenstick versus torus fractures is correct?
o: Greenstick fractures fail on the tension side; torus fractures buckle on the compression side
Torus fractures fail on the tension side
Greenstick fractures fail on the compression side

rounds.t: Metabolic bone disease and avascular necrosis

q.s: A 68-year-old woman has a vertebral compression fracture after lifting groceries. DEXA T-score is −2.9. Serum calcium, phosphate, ALP and PTH are normal. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Low Ca and PO4, high ALP.
Correct. Normal labs with low bone mass.

q.s: Osteoporosis is diagnosed by a DEXA T-score of:
Denosumab treats osteoporosis by:
o: Binding RANKL as a monoclonal antibody

q.s: Which drug class can cause secondary osteoporosis?
e: Correct. Also alcohol, anticonvulsants, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement and PPIs.

q.s: An infant has fractures, anemia, hepatosplenomegaly and blindness from optic nerve compression. X-rays show diffusely dense "bone-in-bone." Which enzyme may be mutated?
Why is bone marrow transplant potentially curative in osteopetrosis?
o: Osteoclasts derive from monocytes, which come from marrow stem cells

q.s: A child with vitamin D deficiency has bowed legs, beading of the costochondral junctions and a soft skull. Which lab pattern is expected?
Why is phosphate low in osteomalacia?
o: Low vitamin D lowers calcium, raising PTH, which causes renal phosphate wasting

q.s: Which x-ray finding is characteristic of osteomalacia in adults?
A 70-year-old man notices his hat no longer fits and has hearing loss. ALP is markedly elevated; calcium, phosphate and PTH are normal. Diagnosis?
Biopsy of a lesion in Paget disease shows:
o: Mosaic pattern of woven and lamellar bone

q.s: Which complications are associated with Paget disease of bone?
e: Correct. AV shunts in bone; malignant transformation.

q.s: The first stage of Paget disease is dominated by which cells?
Which drug class is used to treat Paget disease?
Why is the femoral head prone to avascular necrosis?
o: It is supplied only by the obturator artery
It is supplied by the femoral vein
It is a watershed area supplied mainly by the medial circumflex femoral artery

q.s: Which mnemonic lists causes of avascular necrosis?
e: Correct. Glucocorticoids, alcohol, sickle cell, trauma, SLE, the Bends, Legg-Calvé-Perthes, Gaucher, SCFE.

q.s: A patient with chronic kidney disease has bone pain. Which lab pattern indicates secondary hyperparathyroidism?
o: Normal Ca and PTH with high ALP

q.s: A patient with sarcoidosis has hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia and suppressed PTH. Diagnosis?
Brown tumors are seen in which condition?
o: Osteitis fibrosa cystica from primary hyperparathyroidism

q.s: Osteoporosis most often causes which fractures in addition to vertebral compression fractures?
Which is the most common benign bone tumor?
e: Correct. A lateral bony projection with a cartilage cap, usually near the knee.

q.s: Hereditary multiple exostoses is caused by mutations in:
A 19-year-old man has leg pain that is worse at night and dramatically relieved by aspirin. X-ray shows a small cortical lesion with a radiolucent core. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Larger, vertebrae, no NSAID relief.

q.s: Osteomas on facial bones are associated with:
A 30-year-old woman has knee pain. X-ray shows an expansile, "soap bubble" lesion in the epiphysis of the distal femur. Which cells drive this tumor?
o: Neoplastic mononuclear cells expressing RANKL that recruit osteoclastlike giant cells

q.s: Chondroblastoma typically occurs in:
o: The epiphysis of long bones before skeletal maturation in adolescents
The diaphysis of long bones in children

q.s: A 15-year-old boy has a painful, enlarging mass above the knee. X-ray shows a sunburst pattern and periosteal elevation forming a triangle. Which history increases risk of this tumor?
Osteosarcoma in older adults is often secondary to:
o: Paget disease, prior radiation or bone infarcts

q.s: A 60-year-old man has deep pelvic pain. Imaging shows a lytic medullary lesion with intralesional calcifications and endosteal erosion. Diagnosis?
A 10-year-old boy has a painful femoral shaft mass with fever. X-ray shows an "onion skin" periosteal reaction. Biopsy shows small round blue cells. Which translocation is expected?
e: Correct. Ewing sarcoma, EWS-FLI1 ("11 + 22 = 33," Patrick Ewing's jersey).

q.s: Ewing sarcoma typically arises in the:
o: Diaphysis of long bones and pelvic flat bones

q.s: Which bone tumor occurs in the vertebrae, is >2 cm and does not respond to NSAIDs?
Which is more common in adults than any primary bone tumor?
e: Wrong. Most common benign, but metastases are more common overall.

q.s: Osteosarcoma is composed of:
Osteochondromas point:
Rarely, an osteochondroma transforms into:
Giant cell tumor epidemiology is best described as:
Osteosarcoma most commonly arises in:
o: The metaphysis of long bones around the knee

q.s: Ewing sarcoma is distinguished from lymphoma and chronic osteomyelitis by testing for:
Benign bone tumors that start with the letters "c" and "o" are more common in:

rounds.t: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, and CPPD

q.s: A 68-year-old woman has knee pain that worsens after walking and improves with rest. Morning stiffness lasts 10 minutes. X-ray shows osteophytes and asymmetric joint space narrowing. Diagnosis?
Bony enlargements at the distal interphalangeal joints in osteoarthritis are called:
A 45-year-old woman has symmetric swelling of the MCP, PIP and wrist joints with morning stiffness lasting 2 hours. Which antibody is most specific for her disease?
Rheumatoid factor is:
o: IgM antibody targeting the Fc portion of IgG

q.s: Which HLA type is associated with rheumatoid arthritis?
A patient with long-standing RA has splenomegaly, neutropenia and recurrent infections. Diagnosis?
A coal miner with RA has multiple lung nodules. Diagnosis?
A rheumatoid nodule shows which histology?
Which deformities are characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis?
o: Ulnar deviation, swan neck and boutonniere deformities

q.s: Synovial fluid in osteoarthritis is typically:
A 52-year-old man wakes with a red, hot, swollen first MTP joint after a seafood dinner and several beers. Polarized microscopy of joint fluid would show:
e: Correct. Gout; yellow when parallel to the light.

q.s: Most patients with gout have hyperuricemia due to:
Which drug can precipitate gout by decreasing uric acid excretion?
How does alcohol raise uric acid?
o: Its metabolism raises lactate, which competes with urate and increases urate reabsorption

q.s: Which drug is preferred for long-term urate lowering in a patient who overproduces uric acid?
Gouty tophi most often form on the:
o: External ear, olecranon bursa or Achilles tendon

q.s: A 72-year-old woman has an acutely swollen knee. X-ray shows calcification of the cartilage. Joint fluid shows rhomboid crystals that are blue when parallel to the light. Which condition may be associated?
Which mnemonic describes CPPD crystals?
o: "The blue P's" — blue when parallel, positive birefringence, calcium pyrophosphate, pseudogout

q.s: Which joint is most commonly affected by CPPD?
Systemic inflammation in RA increases the risk of progression of which cardiac condition?

rounds.t: Juvenile arthritis, Sjögren, infection, and spondyloarthritis

q.s: A 7-year-old has daily spiking fevers, a salmon-pink evanescent rash and swelling of both knees and wrists. Which eye complication should be screened for?
A 50-year-old woman has dry, gritty eyes, dry mouth with dental caries, and bilateral parotid swelling. Which antibodies are characteristic?
A patient with Sjögren syndrome develops a progressively enlarging parotid gland. Which complication should be considered?
A pregnant woman with anti-SSA antibodies is at increased risk of having a baby with:
o: Neonatal lupus with congenital heart block

q.s: Which biopsy confirms Sjögren syndrome?
o: Labial salivary gland biopsy showing focal lymphocytic sialadenitis

q.s: A sexually active 22-year-old woman has migratory joint pain, tenosynovitis of the hand and scattered pustules on her wrists. Which organism is most likely?
Synovial fluid in septic arthritis typically shows:
A diabetic man steps on a nail through his sneaker and develops osteomyelitis of the foot. Which organism is classically responsible?
e: Wrong. Most common overall, but not classic here.

q.s: Hematogenous osteomyelitis in children usually affects which part of long bones?
Infection of a prosthetic hip joint is commonly caused by:
e: Wrong. Native joints in young adults.

q.s: The seronegative spondyloarthritides are strongly associated with:
e: Correct. PAIR: psoriatic, ankylosing spondylitis, IBD, reactive.

q.s: A man with psoriasis has swelling of an entire finger ("sausage digit") and nail pitting. X-ray shows a pencil-in-cup deformity at a DIP joint. Diagnosis?
A 26-year-old man has low back pain and stiffness in the morning that improves with exercise. X-ray shows fused vertebrae ("bamboo spine"). Which complications are associated?
o: Uveitis, aortic regurgitation and restrictive lung disease

q.s: Three weeks after a bout of Chlamydia urethritis, a man has knee arthritis, red eyes and dysuria. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. "Can't see, can't pee, can't bend my knee."

q.s: Hyperkeratotic lesions on the palms and soles in reactive arthritis are called:
Which organism is NOT a classic trigger for reactive arthritis?
e: Correct. "She Caught Students Cheating Yesterday": Shigella, Campylobacter, Salmonella, Chlamydia, Yersinia.

q.s: Inflammatory back pain in spondyloarthritis characteristically:
o: Is associated with morning stiffness and improves with exercise

q.s: Inflammation at tendon insertion sites, such as the Achilles, is called:
Septic arthritis treatment includes:
o: Empiric antibiotics, aspiration with Gram stain and drainage

q.s: Which organism causes osteomyelitis in patients with sickle cell anemia?

rounds.t: SLE, antiphospholipid syndrome, myopathies, and IgG4 disease

q.s: A 25-year-old woman has a rash over her cheeks that spares the nasolabial folds, painless mouth ulcers, joint pain and proteinuria. Which antibody is most specific for her disease?
SLE organ damage is primarily caused by which hypersensitivity type?
Deficiency of which complement proteins is associated with SLE?
o: Early components such as C1q, C4 and C2

q.s: What is the most common cause of death in SLE?
e: Wrong. Common, but not most common.
Wrong. Common, but not most common.

q.s: Which valve lesion is associated with SLE?
The most common and severe type of lupus nephritis is:
A patient has features of SLE, scleroderma and polymyositis with a speckled ANA. Which antibody is expected?
A 30-year-old woman with SLE has had three miscarriages and a DVT. Her PTT is prolonged and does not correct with normal plasma. Her VDRL is positive. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibodies.

q.s: What is the treatment for antiphospholipid syndrome with thrombosis?
In muscle wasting from disuse or glucocorticoids, CK is typically:
e: Correct. CK rises in inflammatory myositis.

q.s: A 72-year-old woman has pain and stiffness in her shoulders and hips, worse in the morning, without weakness. ESR is 88 mm/h and CK is normal. What treatment is expected to work rapidly?
Polymyalgia rheumatica is associated with which vasculitis?
A 35-year-old woman has widespread pain, multiple tender points, poor sleep and "brain fog." ESR, CRP and CK are normal. Which treatment is appropriate?
o: Regular exercise and TCAs, SNRIs or gabapentinoids

q.s: A 55-year-old woman has progressive difficulty climbing stairs and combing her hair. She has a violet rash on her eyelids and scaly papules over her knuckles. CK is high. She should be screened for:
o: Small cell lung cancer only for Lambert-Eaton

q.s: Polymyositis differs from dermatomyositis histologically by showing:
o: Perimysial inflammation with CD4+ T cells
Endomysial inflammation with CD8+ T cells

q.s: Which antibody is specific for polymyositis/dermatomyositis and targets histidyl-tRNA synthetase?
A soccer player develops a painful mass in his thigh weeks after a hard kick. Imaging shows eggshell calcification. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. May be mistaken for it.
Correct. Heterotopic ossification after blunt trauma.

q.s: A patient with autoimmune pancreatitis, bilateral salivary gland swelling and retroperitoneal fibrosis has elevated serum levels of which immunoglobulin subclass?
Which thyroid disease is part of IgG4-related disease?
Which features form the "RASH OR PAIN" criteria for SLE?
o: Rash, arthritis, serositis, hematologic disorders, oral ulcers, renal disease, photosensitivity, ANA, immunologic disorder, neurologic disorders

q.s: A 72-year-old woman has a new right-sided headache, jaw pain when chewing and scalp tenderness. ESR is 102 mm/h. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Temporal artery biopsy first, then treat
Start high-dose glucocorticoids immediately, then arrange temporal artery biopsy
e: Correct. Giant cell arteritis risks blindness.

q.s: Blindness in giant cell arteritis results from:
o: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy from ophthalmic artery involvement

q.s: A 28-year-old Asian woman has fever, night sweats, arm claudication and unequal blood pressures in her arms with weak radial pulses. Diagnosis?

A 3-year-old Japanese boy has fever for 6 days, bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, a strawberry tongue, cracked lips, swollen hands and cervical lymphadenopathy. Which complication is most feared?
What is the treatment for Kawasaki disease?
e: Correct. One of the few uses of aspirin in children.

q.s: A middle-aged man with chronic hepatitis B has fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, hypertension and a foot drop. Angiography shows multiple renal and mesenteric microaneurysms. Which organ is typically spared?
e: Correct. Polyarteritis nodosa spares the lungs.

q.s: A 35-year-old man who smokes two packs a day has painful ulcers on his fingertips, Raynaud phenomenon and superficial phlebitis. What is the key treatment?
A patient has hemoptysis, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and palpable purpura, with no upper airway involvement. Kidney biopsy shows pauci-immune GN. MPO-ANCA is positive. Diagnosis?
A patient with long-standing asthma develops eosinophilia, peripheral neuropathy and palpable purpura. Which ANCA pattern is associated?
A 45-year-old has chronic sinusitis, a nasal septum perforation, hemoptysis with lung nodules and hematuria. Which antibody is expected?
A patient with hepatitis C has palpable purpura, arthralgias and weakness. Blood proteins precipitate when cooled. Diagnosis?
A 6-year-old boy has palpable purpura on his buttocks and legs, knee pain and colicky abdominal pain 2 weeks after a cold. Urinalysis shows hematuria. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Purpura is not palpable; no arthritis.

q.s: IgA vasculitis is associated with which abdominal complication?
A patient develops palpable purpura on the legs 8 days after starting a cephalosporin, with no organ involvement. Diagnosis?
A Turkish man has recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis and tender red nodules on his shins. Which HLA type is associated?
A woman with SLE has urticaria that lasts more than 24 hours, purpura and abdominal pain. Labs show low C1q and anti-C1q antibodies. Diagnosis?
Polyarteritis nodosa histology shows:
The "string of pearls" appearance on angiography is characteristic of:

rounds.t: Neuromuscular junction disease, Raynaud, and review

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has drooping eyelids and double vision that worsen through the day, and difficulty chewing by the end of meals. Reflexes are normal. Which structure is targeted by autoantibodies?
Myasthenia gravis is associated with which mediastinal finding?
A 62-year-old smoker has proximal leg weakness that improves after repeated effort, dry mouth, constipation and absent reflexes. Which cancer is associated?
Which feature distinguishes Lambert-Eaton syndrome from myasthenia gravis?
o: Weakness improves with use and reflexes are decreased

q.s: Which drug is used to treat the symptoms of myasthenia gravis?
In the cold, a woman's fingers turn white, then blue, then red. She has no other disease. What is the first-line treatment?
Raynaud phenomenon is caused by:
o: Arteriolar (small-vessel) vasospasm in response to cold or stress

q.s: Digital ulcers with Raynaud phenomenon suggest:
o: Secondary Raynaud syndrome, such as from CREST or SLE

q.s: In myasthenia gravis, ACh receptor antibodies cause weakness because:
o: Fewer functional postsynaptic receptors are available for ACh

q.s: Which mnemonic links the order of Lambert-Eaton and myasthenia gravis to the NMJ anatomy?
o: "L comes before M" — Lambert-Eaton is presynaptic, myasthenia is postsynaptic

q.s: A 58-year-old man has acute knee swelling. Joint fluid shows WBC 85,000/mm³ with gram-positive cocci in clusters. Diagnosis?
Which feature is typical of polymyalgia rheumatica but not polymyositis?
o: Pain and stiffness without weakness and with normal CK

q.s: Which bone disorder has an isolated increase in ALP with normal calcium, phosphate and PTH?
Which vasculitis affects asthmatic patients and causes eosinophilic infiltration?
A 14-year-old boy has knee pain. X-ray shows a lytic lesion crossing the physis in the epiphysis before skeletal maturity. Diagnosis?
Which joints does rheumatoid arthritis typically spare?
e: Correct. RA involves MCP, PIP and wrist.

q.s: An acute gout attack is treated with:
o: Allopurinol started during the attack alone

q.s: A patient with Lambert-Eaton syndrome would show which autonomic symptoms?
Antiphospholipid antibodies can cause which false-positive test?
Which finding on examination is characteristic of myasthenia gravis but not Lambert-Eaton syndrome?
o: Fatigable ptosis and diplopia with preserved reflexes
